2610.06666.title: What Matters for Latent Reasoning with Flow Matching
2610.06666.paper_summary: Latent reasoning lets a large language model (LLM) think in a continuous space and verbalize only the answer. We argue that an effective latent thought must meet five requirements: it should be useful, helping produce the correct answer rather than merely changing it, diverse, so that resampling yields different reasoning trajectories, explainable, so that a decoded chain of thought (CoT) reflects reasoning the answer actually follows, refinable with more inference compute, and efficient, costing less than an explicit CoT at comparable accuracy. Current methods rarely meet these requirements: they learn shortcuts from the question, distill the explicit CoT into their weights, or imitate it one token at a time. We focus on flow matching in a learned latent space, the family we argue is best placed to meet them, and identify the training choices that make it work. The result is Flow-based Latent Reasoning (FLaRe), a simple recipe covering what the latent space encodes and how to shape it, where to train the flow, how to read out the answer, and a final stage of training on the model's own verified thoughts. A probe for each requirement shows that FLaRe improves on prior latent methods in all five. It also compares favorably with them on arithmetic benchmarks, while reaching 97% of the accuracy of explicit CoT at a quarter of its latency.
2610.06666.paper_summary_zh: 潛在推理讓大型語言模型（LLM）在連續空間中思考並僅表達答案。我們認為有效的潛在思考必須滿足五個要求：它應該是有用的，幫助產生正確的答案，而不僅僅是改變它；多樣化，以便重新抽樣產生不同的推理軌跡；可解釋的，以便解碼的思維鏈（CoT）反映出實際遵循的推理；可精煉的，能夠通過更多的推理計算進行改進；以及高效的，成本低於在可比準確度下的明確CoT。目前的方法很少滿足這些要求：它們從問題中學習捷徑，將明確的CoT提煉成其權重，或逐個標記地模仿它。我們專注於在學習的潛在空間中進行流匹配，這個家族我們認為最適合滿足這些要求，並確定使其運作的訓練選擇。結果是基於流的潛在推理（FLaRe），這是一個簡單的配方，涵蓋潛在空間編碼的內容以及如何塑造它，在哪裡訓練流，如何讀取答案，以及在模型自身經過驗證的思維上進行的最後訓練階段。對每個要求的探測顯示，FLaRe在所有五個方面都優於先前的潛在方法。它在算術基準上也與這些方法相比具有優勢，同時在延遲為其四分之一的情況下達到明確CoT的97%準確度。
